Donna di 75 anni. Mammografia bilaterale: 75-year-old woman. Bilateral mammography in two views (CC and MLO). Clinical question not available.

Una massa irregolare ad alta densità con:
An irregular high-density mass with spiculated margins is the most specific mammographic sign of carcinoma (BI-RADS 5: probability of malignancy ≥ 95%).
In this case there are two masses, one per breast, in an almost mirror-image location. The pitfall is “satisfaction of search”: once the first lesion is found, one stops looking and the second is missed. To avoid it, the two breasts are always compared in the same view (RCC with LCC, RMLO with LMLO) and the reading is completed even after the first finding.
Synchronous bilateral breast carcinoma is rare (about 1-3% of carcinomas); every suspicious lesion must nevertheless be biopsied, because the second may be a different tumor and changes the therapy. Before surgery, MRI helps to define the extent in both breasts.
Outcome from the collection: carcinoma in both breasts confirmed by biopsy; Luminal A molecular subtype on the right, not indicated on the left.
Trovata una lesione, continua a cercare:: Once you find one lesion, keep looking: always compare the two breasts in the same view.
